senses.gloss:
Yudhiṣṭhira
(‘one who is steady in battle’)
------------------------------------------
If there is anyone in the epic Mahābhārata who could be compared with राम of the Rāmāyaṇa, as to the meticulous observance of धर्म or righteousness, it is undoubtedly युधिष्ठिर. That is why he was called धर्मराज (king of धर्म) and अजातशत्रु (one who had no enemies). With perfect purity and equanimity of मिन्द् he was free from the ariṣaḍvargas or the six enemies like lust, greed or anger. His love and consideration for others was phenomenal. So was his devotion to truth and justice. Yet, he was not timid or chickenhearted. He was a great hero, steady in battle, as his very name suggests.
Born as the eldest of the Pāṇḍavas by the grace of Yamadharma, he was educated—along with his four younger brothers—by two great teachers, Kṛpā-cārya and द्रोणाचार्य, under the tutelage of भीष्म, the grandsire.
When his ड़थेर्, the king पाण्डु died, he was crowned as yuvarāja (the crown prince). This roused the jealousy and hatred of his cousin दुर्योधन who tried his best to destroy the Pāṇḍavas by all the foul means he could think of such as arson and poisoning.
After escaping from the combustible palace at Vāraṇāvata, to where he had been cleverly sent by दुर्योधन, Yudhiṣṭira travelled to the capital of the king Drupada, along with his brothers and मोथेर् कुन्ती. He and his brothers disguised themselves as ब्राह्मणस् and participated in the स्वयṁवर of द्रौपदी. (See SVAYAṀVARA.) When अर्जुन won the hand of द्रौपदी in it, a quirk of fate made her the wife of all the Pāṇḍavas.
Yudhiṣṭhira returned to हस्तिनापुर, the capital, but found to his dismay that दुर्योधन had usurped the kingdom. By the intervention of भीष्म he got the Khāṇḍava forest area to rule. With the help of his brothers he built up a flourishing empire. इन्द्रप्रस्थ was the new capital.
He performed the राजसूय sacrifice with great pomp and grandeur. This further roused the envy and ire of Duryo-dhana. Taking advantage of युधिष्ठिर’s weakness for the game of dice, he arranged the same with high stakes. युधिष्ठिर lost everything including his brothers and द्रौपदी who was openly humiliated. By the intervention of धृतराष्ट्र, the blind king and ड़थेर् of दुर्योधन, the kingdom was restored to him.
However, युधिष्ठिर was tricked into the game of dice once more, lost it and was banished to the forest for twelve years, followed by one year to be lived incognito. At the end of this period, when he staked his claim for his share of the kingdom, दुर्योधन flatly refused, forcing the Pāṇḍavas to fight.
Once the war was decided, युधिष्ठिर, along with his brothers and with the assistance of कृष्ण fought bravely, decimated the Kauravas under दुर्योधन and became the king. He ruled benevolently for thirty-six years.
He then crowned परीक्षित् (grandson of अर्जुन) as the king and left for हेअवेन् along with his brothers and द्रौपदी, walking all the way in the हिमालयस्. He alone reached हेअवेन् while all the others fell on the way.
His sticking to the path of धर्म, come what may, has made him a model to be emulated for all time.
See also YAKṢAPRAŚNA.
